# Run ledger — P26.11 (surveillance-legislation depth: OpenStates 50-state sweep)

## Spec / Base / Branch / Config

- **Spec:** `docs/tickets/P26.11__surveillance-legislation-depth.md` (SOURCES.10,
  manifest row 108) — deepen the keyed OpenStates path from a single narrow
  `bill_search` seed into the bounded **50-state + DC/territory** sweep:
  keyword-filtered bill queries across every jurisdiction emit typed,
  evidence-backed claims (bill title / status / jurisdiction / session /
  matched keyword) — surveillance-relevant legislation as live claims, not
  just links. A proposed bill is **never** promoted to a §11.14
  `LegalInstrument` claim.
- **Branch:** `devin/p26-11-next-sources` — stacked on
  `devin/p26-10-procurement-portals` (PR #102).
- **Date:** 2026-09-18. Same GCP posture as P26.8–P26.10: user account
  `14stevevitali@gmail.com` on `zeta-medley-508121-u7`; per-job upserts
  (`gcloud run jobs deploy`), never `scheduled-ops.sh --apply`. Local Docker
  daemon unresponsive again — the hosted image was built with **Cloud Build**
  (`gcloud builds submit`, `ops/Dockerfile`, linux/amd64).

## Recon findings (live, 2026-09-17/18 — keyed `X-API-KEY` probes)

| surface | verdict |
|---|---|
| `v3.openstates.org/bills` `per_page` | **max is 20**, not 52 — `per_page=52|53` answers HTTP 400 "invalid per_page, must be in [1, 20]" |
| `v3.openstates.org/jurisdictions` | `per_page=52` accepted; **56 state-classified rows** in 2 pages = 50 states + DC + AS/GU/MP/PR/VI |
| `q=` search | **fuzzy** — `q=facial recognition` returns commemorative resolutions → verbatim match attribution must be LOCAL on the returned record |
| `session=` filter | accepts the index's own identifiers; TX unfiltered 7 hits vs `session=89R` 3 hits (the *called* session `892` must not shadow regular `89R`) |
| session `classification` | values incl. `primary`, `regular`, `special` — the reviewed window is latest-start among `primary`/`regular` |
| throttle | ~10 req/min observed before HTTP 429 → reviewed budget **5/min** pinned through the politeness layer |
| rate | keyless `X-API-KEY` absence → 403 `access_restricted` (P26.4, unchanged) |

## What landed

### 1. The reviewed sweep plan — `openstates_plan.toml` (new, versioned `2026.09.18`)

The whole query plan is **data**, never code (SIG-ENG-001): the two bounded
`/jurisdictions` pages as the discovery surface (52/page = the v3 max, 56 rows
= every state + DC + 5 territories), the `session_window.classes =
["primary","regular"]` latest-start rule (a called/special session never
shadows the main session; a session-less jurisdiction — AS/MP today —
queries unfiltered and records `session=null`), `bills_query.per_page = 20`
(the verified v3 bound), `sort = latest_action_desc`, and
`max_queries = 240` as the hard run bound over the 56×4 = 224 generated
queries. Four reviewed `query_families` (`plates_traffic_enforcement`,
`surveillance_and_monitoring`, `biometric_location_tracking`,
`drones_bodycam_gunshot`) OR their phrases into one bounded `q` per
jurisdiction.

### 2. The reviewed vocabulary — `legislation_vocab.toml` (new, versioned `2026.09.18`)

16 terms extending the P26.6 surveillance set with legislative phrasing —
every ticket-named phrase is covered: `automated license plate`,
`surveillance technology ordinance`, `facial recognition`, `drone`,
`unmanned aerial`, `body-worn camera`, `shotspotter`, `acoustic gunshot`,
`real-time crime`, `cctv`, `automatic traffic enforcement`,
`geofence warrant`, `cell-site simulator`, `stingray`, `data broker`,
`predictive policing`. Each term carries the reviewed `claim_shape`
(`typed_claim` today; `index_only` is the reviewed alternative), regex
`patterns` with word-boundary anchors, and the Part VIII per-datum
`forbidden_tokens` guard applied to every emitted literal — a forbidden
literal is suppressed + recorded, never emitted (§0.7/§43.2).

### 3. Connector — `accountability.py`

- `discover_more` reads the captured `/jurisdictions` index pages (the seed
  targets in `live_targets.toml`) and expands them into ≤240 bounded
  `bill_search` targets — jurisdiction + resolved session + OR-batched
  phrases + `per_page=20` riding the target row as data. Deterministic given
  the same captures (canonical id order); a non-results page is
  `ContentDrift` — fail closed.
- `fetch` sends `X-API-KEY` for **every** openstates target (index + expanded
  bills) — the key resolves from `$SIG_OPENSTATES_KEY` only, never in the
  URL, so no credential lands in source_uri / run rows (HG-09).
- `parse`/`extract` fail closed: an error envelope (`{"detail": …}` — the
  API's rate-limit/error shape answers HTTP 200-class envelopes), malformed
  JSON, or a non-`results` payload is `ContentDrift`, never a fabricated
  bill. Each `bill_index` record carries `row_index` + `retrieved_at`.
- `normalize` — the claim-shape map: a bill whose own title/other_titles
  literally matches a `typed_claim` term emits the bill-surface claim set
  (`bill_external_id`, `bill_identifier`, `bill_title`, `bill_session`,
  `bill_jurisdiction`, `bill_status`, `bill_status_date`, and one
  `bill_matched_keyword` per typed term). Every claim carries the bill
  record URL (official legislature page first, OpenStates record as
  fallback), a `Locator.row` into the captured results array — byte-range
  locator into the named field for keyword claims — and the **verbatim**
  literal as `raw_value`. Claims carry **no `observed_at`** — identity is
  stable record content ("the OpenStates record contains this field"), so
  an unchanged record digests identically on ANY re-run
  (SIG-INGEST-003/017; the atlas optional-`observed_at` pattern). The
  observation time lives on the capture/evidence (`claim_evidence` →
  capture → `retrieved_at`); the record's own `latest_action_date` stays
  verbatim in `bill_status_date` — it is routinely future-dated (scheduled
  votes/hearings) and tripped `claim_observed_not_future` on the first
  hosted run. The sink stamps `observed_unknown_reason` honestly. This is
  also the idempotency the verified 250/day key tier requires: only a
  content-keyed claim dedupes across a next-day rerun. Unmatched bills
  keep the P26.4 `index_only` link unchanged. No volatile field keys a
  claim (no retrieval timestamp, no capture id).
- `bill_query` + `jurisdiction_index` non-claim rows record the sweep's
  honest per-state outcome (matched/empty, counts, truncation when
  `total_items` exceeds the bounded page) — they land on the fetch record's
  `document_outcomes`, not the claim spine.
- A pending bill is never a `LegalInstrument` — `legislative_bill` is the
  entity record of a *proposed* instrument; no enactment is inferred from
  identifier/title/status/latest-action/presence (§3.1).

### 4. Rate-limit wiring — shared politeness layer only

- `api_allowlist.toml`: `rate_limit_per_min = 5` on the
  `v3.openstates.org` row (the reviewed declared budget);
  `api_allowlist.py` exposes `api_allow_entry()`.
- `net.py`: `PoliteFetcher.set_host_delay` pins a host floor on the shared
  `RateLimiter` — **ratchet-up only** (robots' crawl-delay can demand
  slower, never lower the pinned API budget).
- `runner.py`: a `rate_limit_per_min` on any target row pins its host's
  `60/rpm`-second interval before the sweep; `bill_query` rows serialize
  onto `FetchRecord.document_outcomes` (jurisdiction, session, query
  family, totals, indexed/matched, truncated, plan_version).

### 5. live_targets + vocab gate

`live_targets.toml` openstates seed = the two `jurisdictions_index` pages
with `rate_limit_per_min = 5`. `accountability_vocab.toml` →
`vocab_version 2026.09.18`, +9 legislative-bill predicates in the allowlist
(`legislative_bill`, `bill_external_id`, `bill_identifier`, `bill_title`,
`bill_session`, `bill_jurisdiction`, `bill_status`, `bill_status_date`,
`bill_matched_keyword`), `spdx = "CC0-1.0"` on the openstates config.

## Deterministic gate

- `tests/connectors/test_openstates_sweep.py` (19 tests) over the two real
  captured `/jurisdictions` pages (committed fixtures) + the P26.4 bill
  fixture: plan bounds (per_page ≤ 20, max_queries, session classes),
  56-jurisdiction coverage, TX `89R` resolution (never the called `892`),
  AS/MP session-less, per-family target URLs, local verbatim matching vs
  the fuzzy API, typed claims with row/byte-range locators + bill-record
  evidence + verbatim literals, never a LegalInstrument, `index_only`
  fallback, `bill_query`/`jurisdiction_index` outcome rows, fail-closed
  error envelopes + malformed payloads, Part VIII suppression, digest
  stability (no volatile claim fields).
- `tests/connectors/test_net.py`: pinned API budget survives a shorter
  robots crawl-delay; a slower robots delay still wins (ratchet-up).
- `test_promoted_sources.py::test_openstates_bill_index_over_fixture`
  updated for the claim-shape map (both fixture titles match → typed
  claims).
- **inherited-defect fix:** `tests/connectors/fixtures/procportal/
  bonfire_portal_shell.html` carried third-party credential literals
  (Google Maps `AIza…`, reCAPTCHA, ag-Grid license) — `secret_scan.py` was
  red on the base; all three scrubbed to `REDACTED` (HG-09, structure

- `make check` green: lint, format, mypy (231 files), **3274 passed**,
  verify-gen.

## Hosted sweep — `sig-ingest-openstates`

- Cloud Build → `sig-api@sha256:ac235f93…` (first), then
  `sig-api@sha256:50b647c7…` after the `observed_at` fix — linux/amd64 via
  `gcloud builds submit` (`ops/Dockerfile`, repo-root context).
- Job redeployed: `timeoutSeconds 5400` (the ~50-min sweep needed more
  than the unset default), `maxRetries 0`, existing env +
  `SIG_OPENSTATES_KEY=sig-openstates-key` binding unchanged.
- **Execution `nx527` (06:32–07:22, 2,981s ≈ 226 requests at the pinned
  12s interval):** the full 56-jurisdiction × 4-family sweep fetched
  cleanly — then `PgClaimSink` refused the first claim:
  `CheckViolation … claim_observed_not_future` (a bill whose
  `latest_action_date` is a scheduled future action). `outcome=error`,
  `claims_added=0`, the run row records the violation verbatim —
  fail-loud, append-only, nothing half-written. Fixed by the no-observed_at
  commit; captures are container-local so the next run refetches.
- **Executions `jwm5f` (07:37) + `clf7v` (07:52):** both seed
  `/jurisdictions` fetches answered persistent **HTTP 429** — three
  `back_off` retries each (1s→2s→4s) recorded on `rate_limit_events`,
  then recorded as **disappearances** (2 each). No index → zero bill
  queries → `outcome=ok`, `claims_added=0`, ~21s. The rate-limit
  recording path is verified live.
- **Quota discovery (direct keyed probe):** the 429 body is verbatim
  `{"detail":"exceeded limit of 250/day: 343"}` — the key's tier is
  **250 requests/day** and the day's window is exhausted (the ~90
  exploratory probes + the 226-request sweep + retries). A same-day
  sweep + idempotent rerun (452 requests) cannot fit inside one daily
  window — hence the content-only claim digest (a next-day rerun over
  unchanged records dedupes to zero).
- **Sweep + idempotent rerun:** pending the daily-quota window (see
  DEFERRALS row below); the job is deployed and ready.
